header.running_head: The Sanctity of the Blood and Wealth of the Muslims

blocks.text:
'I testify that there is none worthy of worship but Allaah'
However, we did not withdraw from him until we killed him. When we returned to Rasulullaah ﷺ..." The rest of the narration is just like the one quoted above from Ibn Is'haaq.[^1]

Another narration states that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "He professed 'Laa Ilaaha Illallaah' and you still killed him?" Hadhrat Usaama (RA) replied, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ! He said it only for fear of our weapons." Rasulullaah ﷺ asked, "Did you tear open his heart to know whether he said it for that reason or not? Who will defend you against 'Laa Ilaaha Illallaah' on the Day of Qiyaamah?" Hadhrat Usaama (RA) says, "Rasulullaah ﷺ continued repeating the statement until I wished that I had become a Muslim just that day."[^2]
Rasulullaah ﷺ Rebukes Hadhrat Bakr bin Haaritha (RA) as well

Hadhrat Bakr bin Haaritha (RA) narrates, "I was once part of an expedition that Rasulullaah ﷺ dispatched. When we clashed with the Mushrikeen, I attacked a man who sought protection from me by accepting Islaam. I however killed him. When this was reported to Rasulullaah ﷺ, he became very angry and distanced himself from me until Allaah revealed the verse:

blocks.arabic_text: وَمَا كَانَ لِمُؤْمِنٍ اَنْ يَّقْتُلَ مُؤْمِنًا اِلَّا خَطَـًٔا
blocks.text: It is not for (not becoming of) a Mu'min to kill another Mu'min except (unless) by mistake...
(Because I had killed him in error) Rasulullaah ﷺ was then pleased with me and drew me closer."[^3]
Rasulullaah ﷺ Is Cold Towards Someone who Killed a Mu'min

Hadhrat Uqba bin Khaalid Laythi (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ once dispatched an expedition that engaged the enemy in battle. When one of them started to flee, one of the Muslims pursued him with a drawn sword. As the man shouted, "I am a Muslim! I am a Muslim!" the Muslims paid no heed to his cries and killed him with a blow form his sword. When the news reached Rasulullaah ﷺ, he used harsh words to condemn it. These words reached the man who killed and as Rasulullaah ﷺ was delivering a lecture, he stood up and said, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ! I swear by Allaah that he said it only to save himself from being killed." Rasulullaah ﷺ however ignored the man and those in his direction and continued with his lecture. The man repeated himself saying, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ! He said it only to save himself from being killed." Rasulullaah ﷺ again ignored the man and those in his direction and continued with his lecture.
